questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.**

He did not go (1)/ to the newly built temple on foot, (2)/ he went there by the car. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in** 'he went there by the car'.**
 
• Definite article **“the” **needs to be omitted to make the sentence meaningful. 
 
• Here ‘car’ is not mentioned before in the sentence, so there is no specific information about ‘which car’ one is talking about. 
 
• Also “by the car” is not an adverbial phrase. Here “by” would mean ‘near to’ which is inappropriate in this sentence. 
 
• Hence, option 3 is correct.

**Correct sentence:**__ *He did not go to the newly built temple on foot, he went there by car.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No error'**. 

She ascended (1)/ to the throne (2)/ at the early age of seven. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition “**to**” before the term "**the throne**."
 
• In correct usage, "**ascended**" should not be followed by the preposition "**to**".
 
• The correct phrase should be "**ascended the throne**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She ascended **the throne** at the early age of seven."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "She ascended," **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **3: "at the early age of seven."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 2.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option. **

Neha's mother was annoyed with her as she could not _____ her examination.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Get through.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The context of the sentence tells us that Neha's mother was unhappy because of Neha's performance in the exam. It hints that she might have failed in the exam.
 
• "Get off", "get on" and "get through" are all phrases unlike "get upon".
 
• **'Get through'** means to pass or succeed in something.
 
 
• ​**Example**: He **got through** his exams without too much trouble.
 
 
 
• According to the context of the sentence, get through is the most appropriate phrase to be filled in the blank.
 
• Hence, option 4 is correct. 

Correct sentence: Neha's mother was annoyed with her as she could not get through__ her examination. ​ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **'Get off'** means to leave a place; escape a punishment or be acquitted.

 
 
• **Example**: I tripped as I **got off** the bus.
 
 
 
• **'Get on'** means to manage or deal with a situation or have a good relationship. 
 
 
• **Example**: He doesn't **get on** with his daughter.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the word similar in meaning to the word given. **

Ebullient
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Enthusiastic.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Enthusiastic** means feeling or showing strong excitement about something किसी वस्‍तु या कार्य के विषय में) उत्‍साहपूर्ण; उत्तेजना और रुचि से पूर्ण.

 
 
• Ex. The **enthusiastic **crowd cheered and clapped wildly, screaming Donald's name. 
 
 
 
• **Ebullient** means cheerful and full of energy ऊर्जा एवं उत्साह से पूर्ण, जोशिला. 
 
 
• ​Ex. The award winner was in an **ebullient **mood at the dinner in her honor.
 
 
 
• We can see that Enthusiastic and Ebullient are similar in meaning.

**So option 3 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deceitful** means something full of fraud कपटी; बहकाने वाला. 

 
 
• Ex. Anything that involves intentionally misleading someone is **deceitful**.
 
 
 
• **Insincerity **means callous and irresponsible behavior निष्‍ठाहीनता, असत्‍यता. 
 
 
• Ex. He recalled their many past **insincerities**. 
 
 
 
• **Prejudice **is preconceived opinion of somebody or something which might not be correct किस व्‍यक्ति या वस्‍तु के प्रति प्रबल नापसंदगी या अविश्‍वास.
 
 
• Ex. The war against **prejudice **is never-ending.

questions.question: **In the following question, four words are given out of which one word is incorrectly spelt. Find the incorrectly spelt word**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Receeding**". [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The incorrectly spelt word is "Receeding". The correct spelling is "**Receding**".
 
• **Receding**: Receding refers to the act of moving back or withdrawing. It can describe something that is gradually becoming more distant or moving away from a previous position.
 
 
• **Example**: As he looked out at the horizon, he noticed the receding waves as the tide went out.
 
 
 
• Let us look at the meanings of other words:
 
• **Cemetery**: A cemetery is a designated area or plot of land where deceased individuals are buried or interred. It is a place for the respectful remembrance and final resting of the deceased.
 
 
• **Example**: She visited her grandfather's grave at the cemetery and placed fresh flowers on the tombstone.
 
 
 
• **Parallelogram**: A parallelogram is a quadrilateral (a four-sided polygon) in which opposite sides are parallel to each other. It is characterized by its opposite sides being equal in length and opposite angles being equal in measure.
 
 
• **Example**: The shape of the table was a perfect parallelogram, with two pairs of parallel sides.
 
 
 
• **Rehearsal**: A rehearsal is a practice session or run-through of a performance or event before it takes place. It is a preparatory activity where individuals or groups practice their roles, actions, or speeches to ensure a smooth and successful execution.
 
 
• **Example**: The theater cast gathered for a final rehearsal of the play before the opening night.
 
 
 
• Hence option 1 is correct.

questions.question:

Q: Let us consider the village artisans.

R: This will also provide employment to all the educated people of the villages. 

S: Having discussed the problems and requirements of rural life.

Then statement Q is followed which further adds to the requirement of the topic.Statement R of all the statement seems like a well defined conclusion... hence the last sentence in the sequence would be RThis way, statement P is the 3rd statement.

questions.question:
**In the following question, a sentence has been given in Active/Passive voice. Out of four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active voice. **

I saw him leaving the movie theatre.

options.text: He was seen leaving the movie theatre by me
Leaving the movie theatre he was seen by me.
He was seen to be leaving the movie theatre.
He had been seen leaving the movie theatre.

questions.solution: The active voice describes a sentence where the subject performs the action stated by the verb. In passive voice sentences, the subject is acted upon by the verb. Here, the subject is the speaker and he is "seeing" someone which is an action. Then in the conversion, the speaker should be acted upon. But the tense of the statement shouldn't be changed. Option 2 is incorrect due to a grammatical flaw. Option 3 and 4 are incorrect as they are not in the correct context. The appropriate statement is option 1.

questions.question:

The principal said, "Be quiet, girls."

options.text: The principal called the girls and ordered them to be quiet.
The principal commanded the girls that they be quiet.
The principal urged the girls to be quiet
The principal said that the girls should be quiet.

questions.solution: In the direct speech, the principal actually gave an order to the girls. Therefore, even in the indirect speech, the statement should in the form of an order. Nature of the statement should not be changed. This way, option 4 is incorrect. Option 1 is incorrect because it is not mentioned in the active speech that the principal has called the girls too. Option 2 is incorrect due to a grammatical error.
